stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh braces for third intense cyclone in a month
stories.title: Andhra Pradesh braces for third intense cyclone in a month
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: After cyclones Arnab and Murasu, another strong cyclone is headed towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, that too in less than a month.
On Sunday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that a depression had formed in the southeast and adjoining southwest region of the Bay of Bengal.
This system is set to intensify as it tracks northwestwards during the next couple of days.
Once intensified into a cyclone, its will be called Akvan, a name proposed by Iran.
The cyclone development is expected around November 16 and its further land-ward track likely to continue through November 18.
The IMD said, “The system is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of South Bay of Bengal on November 16.
It will further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal on November 17.
Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast during subsequent two days.”

Akvan will be third cyclone to develop in the Bay of Bengal this year and notably, the third in the post-monsoon season to form in the North Indian Ocean basin (comprising the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea).

On Sunday morning, the depression was located about 620 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 680 km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram, 800 km east-southeast of Chennai, 960 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 1,070 km south-southeast of Gopalpur.
The Met department has warned of intense rainfall over coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha in view of the impending cyclone.
Due to squally weather and rough conditons in the high sea, the fishermen community have been warned against venturing into the sea next week.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan may bring rain to Telangana from November 20, IMD forecasts
stories.summary: The IMD has forecast rain in parts of Telangana on November 20 and 21 under the influence of Cyclone Akvan. Several districts may receive thundershowers and isolated heavy rainfall, while Hyderabad is likely to experience showers from November 21.

stories.headline: The Election Before The Election In Uttar Pradesh
stories.title: The Election Before The Election In Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: Moving away from overall numbers, however, parties are concerned with the impact of deletions on their politically defined constituencies. Yogi Adityanath has now claimed that 1.27 crore Hindu voters have been deleted. If the chief minister’s estimate of ‘deleted Hindu voters’ is correct then who are the rest of the deleted voters varying from 77 lakh to 1.6 crore?

stories.headline: EC tells SC voters left out of draft rolls can reapply without prosecution
stories.title: EC tells SC voters left out of draft rolls can reapply without prosecution
stories.summary: The Election Commission has told the Supreme Court that voters missing from draft electoral rolls despite previous enrolment can reapply through Form 6 without prosecution, provided they are not registered in another constituency and meet the applicable legal requirements
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that voters whose names are missing from draft electoral rolls despite having been enrolled earlier can apply afresh through Form 6 without fear of prosecution.
In an affidavit filed before the court, the poll panel said Chief Electoral.
Officers (CEOs) had been asked to give wide publicity to the clarification, including in local languages.

“It had been brought to the notice of the Commission that some apprehensions were expressed that applicants who were enrolled as voters in previous electoral roll(s) but whose names did not appear in the draft Electoral Roll during the SIR — by filing Form 6, may face action for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, on account of the fact that they were enrolled as voters in the previous electoral roll(s).

“In order to allay such misapprehensions, the Commission… has clarified that no prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely on the ground that the applicant/elector was previously enrolled in the electoral roll(s) prior to the SIR and their name did not appear in the draft electoral roll during the SIR, provided that applicant/elector is not already enrolled in any other Parliamentary or Assembly Constituency and the declaration made is otherwise in accordance with law,” the affidavit said.

The poll panel submitted that it had also taken note of the Supreme Court’s suggestion to reach out to left-out ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate) voters to facilitate their inclusion in the electoral roll.
“The Commission decided to take certain further measures in the interest of the voters.
The Commission has inter alia issued directions by its communication dated November 6, 2026, to the Chief Electoral Officers of the states/UTs where the SIR is ongoing,” it said.
The EC said it had asked the CEOs to allow voters to submit duly filled Enumeration Forms (Annexure.
A) to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Booth Level Officer (BLO) for their current ordinary residence.
“Electors who have not shifted may submit the signed Enumeration Form (Annexure A) with the Annexure-B statement giving the reason for the earlier non-submission of the Enumeration Form.
They can submit it to the ERO/AERO/BLO in person or through family members.
